I do not think that an AI is copy-able. Or rather, I do not believe we will ever be able to copy or transfer consciousness. Certainly not trivially, and potentially just flat-out impossible. I believe it is intrinsically too tied up in the deep structure of the environment said consciousness is running in. Everything up to and including the particular pattern of noise that the cells of your optic nerves make. Or the exact delay between your heart beating and blood pressure changing elsewhere.

Ever seen the experiment where a machine learning algorithm was connected to a FPGA and taught to recognize someone speaking "stop" and "go"? It worked, and worked well. But didn't even work on another copy of the same FPGA. Seemingly unconnected components that it doesn't work without. And I believe consciousness is the same way. Too many subtle/fractal/chaotic details to be able to actually copy things.

Have you seen people on drugs looping? Consciousness doesn't need to be so exact to be a replicate. People act in the same ways and patterns even when their consciousness isn't exactly the same. I agree that no exact copy can be made, but I don't believe that prohibits transfer of consciousness.

That does present complications, I was trying to make the point it doesnt have to be an exact copy to behave in the same way. When I think of how fast computers are advancing, I think it's only a matter of time before the entire complexity of the human brain can be simulated 100% digitally inside a program--and go beyond that and combine conciousnesses to form even larger intelligent networks. I can only speculate. More to the issue of transferring conciousness is we aren't sure how close the copy needs to be. The closer we get it, the more information we need from the host.
